tagline: Extending and testing the Kiraly and Tokai dictionary of the Rohonc Codex
intro:
The Rohonc Codex is a small paper book of the sixteenth century. It contains about 450 leaves and is kept at the Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences in Budapest. It is written in a script that occurs in no other document. The writing runs right to left and uses several hundred signs.

Levente Zoltan Kiraly and Gabor Tokai established what the book contains. They identified the apocryphal Life of Adam and Eve running into the legend of the Rood, the story of Joachim and Anne, a Passion the codex itself says it takes from Matthew and John, sermons and parables for the gospels of the year, the Finding of the Cross, the Acts of the Apostles, and at the end a few pages of one man's diary. The frame is a revelation where an angel of God speaks and the prophet Elijah is the one addressed.

This project started from Kiraly and Tokai's dictionary. It tested and extended their work. It read signs their dictionary leaves undefined, checked every reading at every place the sign stands in the book, and rendered the whole manuscript into English with every word marked by how well it is known.
how_far: The manuscript contains 29,997 words. The project reads 93.4% of them. The figures below show how far the reading goes.
tiers: The dictionary of added readings is sorted into tiers. Tier A survives every place the sign stands in the book, or is proved by an identical formula or a numeral. Tier B survives most places, with the rest unclear rather than against. Tiers C and D are read from one passage with nothing inside the book able to refuse them. Tier G is a guess, printed in brackets, and counted as read nowhere. Withdrawn readings stay in the file with the reason they went.
new_here_lead: The following paragraph describes what is new in this project and what is not.
is_it_true: The project designed tests to break its own readings. Two outside reviewers were shown the write-up and asked what tests they would require; those were run as specified. The summary of results is below.

edition: The whole manuscript is being set as a book in two parts. It will be a continuous retelling by episode alongside all 441 folios with their marked lines. It is being finished and will appear in the OONA Free Library. Nothing on this site waits on it.
credit: The manuscript is out of copyright. Kiraly and Tokai's dictionary, transcription and page images are theirs. They are credited on every page and linked, not rehosted. The readings, tests, English and editorial matter are this project's own. Every figure on the site is read out of a saved run, never typed by hand.
reading_lead: This page presents one paragraph of English for each of the 441 folios, in Kiraly and Tokai's page order. Restorations are in brackets. The full per-word marks are in the edition and the rendering, not on this page.
dictionary_lead:
This dictionary contains the 1,787 readings this project added to Kiraly and Tokai's work. It does not reproduce their own 841 entries. The signs are written as glyph codes, using three hexadecimal digits per glyph. The drawn signs are on Kiraly and Tokai's site.

You can search by reading or by sign. You can filter by tier. Each entry shows its evidence line. The dictionary includes tiers A, B, C, D, and G, and withdrawn readings.
data_lead: This page provides every file the site pages are built from. You can download the dictionary and folio English as JSON, the rendering, the reader's edition, every saved run, and the outside readers' replies.

card_script: Learn about the script of the Rohonc Codex.
script_intro:
The writing of the Rohonc Codex runs right to left. The codex dates itself 1593. It is logographic. A sign stands for a word or a whole phrase, not a sound. Kiraly and Tokai established this. Several hundred signs are in use.

Where the signs came from is not settled. This project does not claim to know. The script occurs in no other document. A logographic script is not tied to any one language, since a sign meaning 'Lord' can be voiced in whatever the reader speaks. That is an argument from the structure of the script, not a tested result.
script_signs: The shuffler below shows one sign at a time with its reading.
script_numerals: Numerals are strokes that add. A 'ten' written after a group multiplies that group by ten. This was checked four times. Ten-ten-ten-ten is forty at the forty days and forty nights. Two-two-ten is also forty at the forty days of rain. Six-two is eight at the circumcision on the eighth day. Six-six is twelve at the twelve apostles.
script_phrases: Phrases are written without a space. The example from folio 137v is 'sin, without, Jesus, conceive, you-Mary', where you-Mary is a single sign. This project confirmed the construction independently of Kiraly and Tokai's glosses and applied it across the book.
script_marks: The marks in the rendering have these meanings. A plain word is read. A word with * was read from one passage with nothing in the book able to refuse it. A word in [brackets] is a restoration and is counted as read nowhere. A hyphen inside a word means one sign read as the smaller signs it is built from. A ~ marks a spelling their own apparatus files as a variant.
script_plates: Twenty-six folios carry pictures, 49 pictures in all. The plates in this edition were redrawn by an image model from the library's low-resolution scan, because no print-quality scan is available. They are new drawings that follow the scribe's composition, not reproductions.
credit_line: This project rests on the dictionary of Kiraly and Tokai; their translation is unpublished. The readings here are this project's own.
